trace_issues.message: Agent 2: line 1 has '*' in column 8; treated as a comment, not program text.
Agent 3: FD BATCH-CONTROL-FILE and FD PROCESS-SEQ-FILE records come from COPY BCHCTL and COPY PRCSEQ; PRCSEQ supplies PROCESS-SEQUENCE-RECORD and STANDARD-SEQUENCES.
Agent 3 (copybook BCHCON): BCT-EMERGENCY PIC X(8) has VALUE 'EMERGENCY' (9 characters). The field is not referenced by RCVPRC00.

Both READ NEXT loops on BATCH-CONTROL-FILE perform 2100-RECOVER-PROCESS, which issues a keyed READ (line 163) and a REWRITE (lines 210/222/234) on the same file. These statements also set WS-BCT-STATUS (the loop condition field) and, with ACCESS MODE DYNAMIC, the keyed READ changes the position used by the next READ NEXT. Loop progress and termination therefore depend on the keys read inside 2100. !! REVIEW
Each loop ends only when WS-BCT-STATUS = '10'; a READ NEXT that fails with another status takes neither AT END nor NOT AT END and the loop repeats.

WS-RECOVERY-MODE is set during the INIT call (1300-SET-RECOVERY-MODE) and tested during the RECV call (2000-PROCESS-RECOVERY); the RECV path relies on WORKING-STORAGE keeping its value between calls. EVALUATE WS-RECOVERY-MODE has no WHEN OTHER: any other value does nothing.
Static CALL 'ERRPROC' USING ERR-MESSAGE in 9000-ERROR-ROUTINE and 3100-UPDATE-FINAL-STATUS; external program, not traced into.

program_narrative: RCVPRC00 is a batch subprogram (PROCEDURE DIVISION USING LS-RECOVERY-REQUEST, ends with GOBACK) that recovers batch processes recorded in BATCH-CONTROL-FILE. The caller selects one function per call: INIT opens BATCH-CONTROL-FILE (I-O) and PROCESS-SEQ-FILE (input), validates that a processing date is present and that the recovery type is 'P' (one process), 'S' (all processes of the date) or 'A' (all processes), and stores the recovery mode, requiring a process ID for process recovery. RECV runs the selected recovery: for one process it reads the control record and the process definition, then restarts the process when its definition is restartable (status READY, restart count plus one, attempt timestamp), terminates it when the restart count exceeds BCT-MAX-RESTARTS (status ERROR, return code BCT-RC-ERROR), or bypasses it otherwise (status DONE, return code BCT-RC-WARNING), and rewrites the control record; sequence and all-process recovery scan the control file from the start and apply the same process recovery to each record read (sequence mode only for records of the processing date). TERM logs a completion message through ERRPROC ('Recovery completed successfully' when the return code is zero, otherwise 'Recovery completed with errors') and closes both files. Error conditions handled: invalid function code, missing date, invalid recovery type, missing process ID, open and close failures, READ/START/REWRITE invalid keys; each performs 9000-ERROR-ROUTINE, which sets BCT-RC-ERROR and calls ERRPROC, after which processing continues.

paragraphs.name: 0000-MAIN
pseudocode: -- Entry point: dispatch on the function code passed by the caller in LS-RECOVERY-REQUEST
SET RETURN-CODE = ls_return_code  -- RETURN-CODE special register: program return code seen by the caller
paragraphs.pseudocode_text:
-- Entry point: dispatch on the function code passed by the caller in LS-RECOVERY-REQUEST
SELECT CASE function_code (LS-FUNCTION)
  WHEN 'INIT' (FUNC-INIT):
    CALL 1000-initialize-recovery
  WHEN 'RECV' (FUNC-RECV):
    CALL 2000-process-recovery
  WHEN 'TERM' (FUNC-TERM):
    CALL 3000-terminate-recovery
  ELSE:
    SET error_text = 'Invalid function code'
    CALL 9000-error-routine
END SELECT
SET RETURN-CODE = ls_return_code  -- RETURN-CODE special register: program return code seen by the caller
RETURN to caller  -- GOBACK

annotations.note: RETURN-CODE is a COBOL special register, not a data item; it is not looked up in the field registry.

paragraphs.name: 1000-INITIALIZE-RECOVERY
pseudocode: -- INIT function: open files, validate the request, set the recovery mode
paragraphs.pseudocode_text:

paragraphs.name: 2000-PROCESS-RECOVERY
pseudocode: -- RECV function: run the recovery selected at INIT time
WHEN 'S':  -- all processes of the processing date
END SELECT  -- no WHEN OTHER: any other mode does nothing
paragraphs.pseudocode_text:
-- RECV function: run the recovery selected at INIT time
SELECT CASE recovery_mode (WS-RECOVERY-MODE)
  WHEN 'P':  -- single process
    CALL 2100-recover-process
  WHEN 'S':  -- all processes of the processing date
    CALL 2200-recover-sequence
  WHEN 'A':  -- all processes
    CALL 2300-recover-all
END SELECT  -- no WHEN OTHER: any other mode does nothing

annotations.note: WS-RECOVERY-MODE is set only in 1300-SET-RECOVERY-MODE during the INIT call; this RECV path relies on WORKING-STORAGE keeping the value between calls.

paragraphs.name: 9000-ERROR-ROUTINE
pseudocode: -- Common error handler: identify the program, set the error return code, log the error
SET ls_return_code = BCT-RC-ERROR  -- error threshold constant from copybook BCHCON (VALUE +8)
PASSING: err_message (ERR-MESSAGE record from copybook ERRHAND)
paragraphs.pseudocode_text:
-- Common error handler: identify the program, set the error return code, log the error
SET err_program = 'RCVPRC00'
SET ls_return_code = BCT-RC-ERROR  -- error threshold constant from copybook BCHCON (VALUE +8)
CALL program ERRPROC
  PASSING: err_message (ERR-MESSAGE record from copybook ERRHAND)

annotations.note: Static CALL to external program ERRPROC (not traced into). The routine has no STOP RUN or GOBACK: control returns to the performing paragraph and processing continues after every error.

paragraphs.name: 1100-OPEN-FILES
paragraphs.pseudocode_text:
OPEN BATCH-CONTROL-FILE for READ-WRITE
IF bct_file_status != '00' THEN
  SET error_text = 'Error opening control file'
  CALL 9000-error-routine
END IF
OPEN PROCESS-SEQ-FILE for READ-ONLY
IF psr_file_status != '00' THEN

paragraphs.name: 1200-VALIDATE-REQUEST
paragraphs.pseudocode_text:
-- Validate the recovery request
IF ls_process_date is blank (SPACES) THEN
  SET error_text = 'Process date required'
  CALL 9000-error-routine
END IF
SELECT CASE recovery_type (LS-RECOVERY-TYPE)
  WHEN 'P', 'S', 'A':
    -- valid type: do nothing (CONTINUE)
  ELSE:
    SET error_text = 'Invalid recovery type'
    CALL 9000-error-routine
END SELECT

annotations.note: Validation errors do not stop INIT; 1300-SET-RECOVERY-MODE still runs with the invalid value.

paragraphs.name: 1300-SET-RECOVERY-MODE
pseudocode: IF recovery_mode is single process ('P', WS-RECOVER-PROCESS) AND ls_process_id is blank THEN
SET error_text = 'Process ID required for process recovery'
paragraphs.pseudocode_text:
SET recovery_mode = ls_recovery_type
IF recovery_mode is single process ('P', WS-RECOVER-PROCESS) AND ls_process_id is blank THEN
  SET error_text = 'Process ID required for process recovery'
  CALL 9000-error-routine
END IF

paragraphs.name: 2100-RECOVER-PROCESS
pseudocode: -- Recover one process: read its control record, decide the action, apply it
READ record from BATCH-CONTROL-FILE where key = bct_key
IF record not found (INVALID KEY) THEN
paragraphs.pseudocode_text:
-- Recover one process: read its control record, decide the action, apply it
SET bct_job_name = ls_process_id
SET bct_process_date = ls_process_date
READ record from BATCH-CONTROL-FILE where key = bct_key
IF record not found (INVALID KEY) THEN
  SET error_text = 'Process record not found'
  CALL 9000-error-routine
END IF
CALL 2110-determine-action
CALL 2120-execute-recovery

annotations.note: BCT-KEY is BCT-JOB-NAME + BCT-PROCESS-DATE + BCT-SEQUENCE-NO (copybook BCHCTL); BCT-SEQUENCE-NO is not set before the keyed READ.
After INVALID KEY the paragraph still determines and executes a recovery action (including a REWRITE) on the record area contents.

paragraphs.name: 2110-DETERMINE-ACTION
pseudocode: -- Decide restart, terminate or bypass from the process definition and restart count
READ record from PROCESS-SEQ-FILE where key = psr_key (psr_process_id + psr_version)
IF record not found (INVALID KEY) THEN
IF process is restartable (psr_restart = 'Y', PSR-RESTARTABLE) THEN
SET recovery_action = RESTART ('R')  -- SET WS-ACTION-RESTART TO TRUE
SET recovery_action = TERMINATE ('T')  -- SET WS-ACTION-TERMINATE TO TRUE
SET recovery_action = BYPASS ('B')  -- SET WS-ACTION-BYPASS TO TRUE
paragraphs.pseudocode_text:
-- Decide restart, terminate or bypass from the process definition and restart count
SET psr_process_id = ls_process_id
READ record from PROCESS-SEQ-FILE where key = psr_key (psr_process_id + psr_version)
IF record not found (INVALID KEY) THEN
  SET error_text = 'Process definition not found'
  CALL 9000-error-routine
END IF
IF process is restartable (psr_restart = 'Y', PSR-RESTARTABLE) THEN
  SET recovery_action = RESTART ('R')  -- SET WS-ACTION-RESTART TO TRUE
ELSE IF bct_restart_count > BCT-MAX-RESTARTS (constant 3) THEN
  SET recovery_action = TERMINATE ('T')  -- SET WS-ACTION-TERMINATE TO TRUE
ELSE
  SET recovery_action = BYPASS ('B')  -- SET WS-ACTION-BYPASS TO TRUE
END IF

annotations.note: Only PSR-PROCESS-ID is set before the keyed READ; PSR-VERSION (second part of PSR-KEY) keeps whatever value the record area holds.

88-level PSR-RESTARTABLE is true when PSR-RESTART = 'Y' (copybook PRCSEQ). A restartable process is always restarted; the restart limit is only checked for non-restartable processes. BCT-MAX-RESTARTS has VALUE 3 in copybook BCHCON.

paragraphs.name: 2120-EXECUTE-RECOVERY
pseudocode: IF recovery_action = RESTART THEN  -- EVALUATE TRUE WHEN WS-ACTION-RESTART
paragraphs.pseudocode_text:
-- Apply the chosen recovery action
IF recovery_action = RESTART THEN  -- EVALUATE TRUE WHEN WS-ACTION-RESTART
  CALL 2121-restart-process
ELSE IF recovery_action = BYPASS THEN
  CALL 2122-bypass-process
ELSE IF recovery_action = TERMINATE THEN
  CALL 2123-terminate-process
END IF  -- no WHEN OTHER

paragraphs.name: 2121-RESTART-PROCESS
pseudocode: -- Restart: put the process back to READY and count the restart
SET current_time = system timestamp  -- ACCEPT WS-CURRENT-TIME FROM TIME STAMP (see annotation)
UPDATE existing batch_control_record in BATCH-CONTROL-FILE  -- REWRITE
paragraphs.pseudocode_text:
-- Restart: put the process back to READY and count the restart
SET bct_status = BCT-STAT-READY  -- constant 'R'
INCREMENT bct_restart_count BY 1
SET current_time = system timestamp  -- ACCEPT WS-CURRENT-TIME FROM TIME STAMP (see annotation)
SET bct_attempt_ts = current_time
UPDATE existing batch_control_record in BATCH-CONTROL-FILE  -- REWRITE
IF rewrite error (INVALID KEY) THEN
  SET error_text = 'Error updating control record'
  CALL 9000-error-routine
END IF

annotations.note: Recorded verbatim: 'ACCEPT WS-CURRENT-TIME FROM TIME STAMP'. TIME STAMP is not a standard ACCEPT source (DATE, DAY, DAY-OF-WEEK, TIME); its exact content depends on the compiler. !! REVIEW

paragraphs.name: 2122-BYPASS-PROCESS
pseudocode: -- Bypass: mark the process DONE with a warning return code
UPDATE existing batch_control_record in BATCH-CONTROL-FILE  -- REWRITE
paragraphs.pseudocode_text:
-- Bypass: mark the process DONE with a warning return code
SET bct_status = BCT-STAT-DONE  -- constant 'D'
SET bct_return_code = BCT-RC-WARNING  -- constant +4
SET bct_error_desc = 'Process bypassed by recovery'
UPDATE existing batch_control_record in BATCH-CONTROL-FILE  -- REWRITE
IF rewrite error (INVALID KEY) THEN
  SET error_text = 'Error updating control record'
  CALL 9000-error-routine
END IF

paragraphs.name: 2123-TERMINATE-PROCESS
pseudocode: -- Terminate: mark the process in ERROR with an error return code
UPDATE existing batch_control_record in BATCH-CONTROL-FILE  -- REWRITE
paragraphs.pseudocode_text:
-- Terminate: mark the process in ERROR with an error return code
SET bct_status = BCT-STAT-ERROR  -- constant 'E'
SET bct_return_code = BCT-RC-ERROR  -- constant +8
SET bct_error_desc = 'Process terminated by recovery'
UPDATE existing batch_control_record in BATCH-CONTROL-FILE  -- REWRITE
IF rewrite error (INVALID KEY) THEN
  SET error_text = 'Error updating control record'
  CALL 9000-error-routine
END IF

paragraphs.name: 2200-RECOVER-SEQUENCE
pseudocode: -- Recover every control record of the processing date
POSITION BATCH-CONTROL-FILE at the first record with key > bct_key  -- COBOL START
IF no record with such a key (INVALID KEY) THEN
SET error_text = 'No processes found for date'
paragraphs.pseudocode_text:
-- Recover every control record of the processing date
SET bct_process_date = ls_process_date
SET bct_job_name = MIN_VALUE  -- LOW-VALUES
POSITION BATCH-CONTROL-FILE at the first record with key > bct_key  -- COBOL START
IF no record with such a key (INVALID KEY) THEN
  SET error_text = 'No processes found for date'
  CALL 9000-error-routine
END IF
WHILE bct_file_status != '10' DO
  READ next record from BATCH-CONTROL-FILE
  IF end of file THEN
    SET bct_file_status = '10'
  ELSE
    IF bct_process_date = ls_process_date THEN
      CALL 2100-recover-process
    END IF
  END IF
END WHILE

annotations.note: BCT-KEY starts with BCT-JOB-NAME (set to LOW-VALUES), so the START positions at the beginning of the file, not at the processing date; the date filter is applied per record at line 256. BCT-SEQUENCE-NO is not set before the START.

2100-RECOVER-PROCESS uses LS-PROCESS-ID (not the job name of the record just read): every matching record triggers recovery of the process ID supplied by the caller. It also issues a keyed READ and a REWRITE on BATCH-CONTROL-FILE inside this READ NEXT loop (see trace_issues nested_io_in_sequential_scan). !! REVIEW

paragraphs.name: 2300-RECOVER-ALL
pseudocode: -- Recover every control record in the file
POSITION BATCH-CONTROL-FILE at the first record with key > bct_key  -- COBOL START
IF no record with such a key (INVALID KEY) THEN
SET ls_process_id = bct_job_name  -- recover the job of the record just read
paragraphs.pseudocode_text:
-- Recover every control record in the file
SET bct_key = MIN_VALUE  -- LOW-VALUES
POSITION BATCH-CONTROL-FILE at the first record with key > bct_key  -- COBOL START
IF no record with such a key (INVALID KEY) THEN
  SET error_text = 'No processes found'
  CALL 9000-error-routine
END IF
WHILE bct_file_status != '10' DO
  READ next record from BATCH-CONTROL-FILE
  IF end of file THEN
    SET bct_file_status = '10'
  ELSE
    SET ls_process_id = bct_job_name  -- recover the job of the record just read
    CALL 2100-recover-process
  END IF
END WHILE

annotations.note: LS-PROCESS-ID is a LINKAGE field: the caller's process ID is overwritten with each job name read.

2100-RECOVER-PROCESS reads the control record with key job name + LS-PROCESS-DATE (the caller's date, not the date of the record just read) and rewrites it inside this READ NEXT loop (see trace_issues nested_io_in_sequential_scan). !! REVIEW

paragraphs.name: 3100-UPDATE-FINAL-STATUS
pseudocode: PASSING: err_message (ERR-MESSAGE record from copybook ERRHAND)
paragraphs.pseudocode_text:
-- Log the overall recovery result
IF ls_return_code = 0 THEN
  SET error_text = 'Recovery completed successfully'
ELSE
  SET error_text = 'Recovery completed with errors'
END IF
CALL program ERRPROC
  PASSING: err_message (ERR-MESSAGE record from copybook ERRHAND)

annotations.note: RCVPRC00 never sets LS-RETURN-CODE to zero; the test relies on the value supplied by the caller or set to BCT-RC-ERROR by 9000-ERROR-ROUTINE in this call.
Static CALL to external program ERRPROC (not traced into); ERR-PROGRAM is set only by 9000-ERROR-ROUTINE, so it may hold a value from an earlier error or none.

CLOSE BATCH-CONTROL-FILE and PROCESS-SEQ-FILE
IF bct_file_status != '00' OR psr_file_status != '00' THEN
